ideas.description: Exploit: make Muon cheap at equal math. Start from E025 (commit 50d39d6: E024 tip plus Muon on the block conv filters, lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, nesterov; 0.7622 at 7.26 s). Change only how the Muon update is implemented, not what it computes. (a) Group the same-shape conv filters (block-2 conv2/conv3, block-3 conv2/conv3, and any others that match) and run Newton-Schulz on each stacked group as one batched bf16 bmm. (b) Put the whole Muon step (momentum update, nesterov blend, NS, renorm, param update) into the same compiled function as the fused foreach SGD+Lookahead update, inside the CUDA-graph-captured train step. Read the LR from the GPU step table. Momentum buffers stay persistent, are captured in build on synthetic data, and are zeroed in prepare. Check in a short synthetic test that the parameter delta matches E025's per-parameter loop to bf16 tolerance.
ideas.expected: The ~2.3 ms/step of Muon overhead falls to ~0.6-1.0 ms/step, the NS matmul floor (a 704x6336 NS is ~0.25 ms). Time drops from 7.26 s to ~6.65-6.85 s. Accuracy is unchanged within noise at ~0.758-0.765. If time is <= 6.45 s it is a new best outright. Otherwise it is the base for the Muon epoch cut, where each epoch saved is worth ~0.6 s. If time stays > 7.0 s, NS compute rather than launch overhead dominates, and the next thing to try is fewer NS iterations.

ideas.description: Exploit: spend Muon's accuracy gain on epochs. Start from the I032 result if it was kept as the Muon base, otherwise from E025 (commit 50d39d6). Change only the epoch count, from 11 to 9.5. Rescale the LR, Lookahead and Muon schedules to the new step count so they still anneal fully, and keep the 24 px phase at the first 50% of steps. Report per-seed accuracy. If the 3-seed mean margin over 0.753 is under 0.3 pp, rerun once and pool before promoting it (H1.1.3 rule).
ideas.expected: Muon gave +0.78 pp, about 1.5 epochs' worth at ~0.52 pp/epoch near 10-11 ep (E020). Accuracy ~0.751-0.758, centred near 0.755. Time scales with steps: ~6.27 s from the E025 base, or ~5.7-5.9 s from a fused I032 base. Either is a new best if feasible (tip 6.45 s). If accuracy lands at 0.749-0.753, Muon's per-epoch slope is steeper than SGD's, and the follow-up is 10 epochs.

ideas.description: Exploit throughput along the batch axis. On the tip E024 (128/256/704, 50% of steps at 24 px with antialias, translate 2, LS 0.1, alternating flip, batch 1536, fused foreach SGD+Lookahead, 11 epochs), change only the batch size, from 1536 to 2048. Hold the per-example LR and wd fixed (per-step LR x4/3), tie the warmup/decay and Lookahead schedule to the new step count, recapture the CUDA graphs for both resolutions in build, and handle the last partial batch the same way as now.
ideas.expected: Time -2 to -4%, from 6.45 s to ~6.2-6.3 s, since fixed per-step overhead is spread over 25% fewer steps (~268 total). Accuracy -0.0 to -0.35 pp. The regime is sample-limited (E015, E024), but steps fall to ~24 per epoch, close to where step-limitation could show. Feasible is a new best, and the batch should then also carry over to the Muon line, where per-step NS cost is amortized the same way. A time gain under 1.5% means the GPU is saturated at 1536, which closes the batch axis.

ideas.description: Explore a schedule constant left over from 37-epoch runs. On the tip E024, change only whiten_bias_epochs, from 3 to 0.5: train the whitening-conv bias for the first 0.5 epochs, then freeze it, with everything else unchanged. First confirm in the code what the current value and semantics are. If the whitening bias is never trained in the current code, record the idea as a no-op and do not run it.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (+/- 0.03 s). Accuracy -0.2 to +0.35 pp, direction uncertain. Training the whitening bias for 27% of an 11-epoch run may perturb the input distribution BN sees during the 24 px phase. A gain >= 0.3 pp banks margin for the 70%-at-24 px or epoch-cut follow-ups and supports H4.5. A change within +/-0.15 pp closes this constant.

ideas.description: Explore the head feature-dimension mechanism without extra conv FLOPs. On the tip E024, change only the global pooling before the linear head: concatenate global max pooling and global average pooling of the block-3 output (704 -> 1408 head input), keeping the head scaling convention. The eval path must handle the same pooling for any B in 1..1024.
ideas.expected: Time +0.0 to +1% (~+0.03 s). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.4 pp. A gain >= 0.3 pp supports H5.2: the 100-way head is limited by its pooled feature dimension, and the block-3 widening gain (E021) is partly a head effect, so it can be bought more cheaply. A gain under 0.15 pp weakens H5.2 and makes the 1x1-expansion test (H5.2.1) low priority.

ideas.description: Block-3 dose-response, as a margin source for the resize line. On the tip E024, change only block-3 width, from 704 to 896 (3 convs per block, head input widened to match). Nothing else changes.
ideas.expected: Time +0.3 to +0.45 s, to ~6.75-6.9 s. Accuracy +0.15 to +0.4 pp. Rate >= 0.75 pp/s supports H1.2.4 and justifies pairing 896 with 70%-at-24 px (H3.2.5). A rate under 0.5 pp/s means block-3 width saturates near 704, and Muon (0.96 pp/s even unfused) is the better margin source.

ideas.description: Exploit fixed per-step host overhead. On the tip E024, capture each resolution phase of training as one CUDA graph instead of replaying a per-step graph from Python. At the start of timed train, large batched kernels stage the augmented, index-gathered batches for the phase into persistent per-step buffers (flip, translate and interpolate done there). The LR and Lookahead alpha are read from the GPU table, and Lookahead uses _foreach_lerp_ in the graph. Capture both phase graphs in build on synthetic data of the real shapes. prepare resets params, buffers, slow weights and the step counter.
ideas.expected: Time -3 to -6%, to ~6.05-6.25 s, by removing host gaps between replays. The 24 px phase gains more, so the 24/32 px step-cost ratio drops from ~0.68 toward <= 0.62. Accuracy unchanged within noise (same math; augmentation RNG stream changes). Gains under 2% mean host gaps are already hidden, which closes H2.4's remaining overhead claim.

structured_output.summary:
The queue was empty: every earlier idea was done or dropped, so there was nothing to drop. I added 7 new ideas.

The current best feasible run is E024: 0.7544 accuracy at 6.448 s, with 128/256/704 widths, 50% of steps at 24 px, batch 1536 and a fused SGD update. That is only 0.14 pp above the 0.753 bar. The run descriptions for E024 and E025 say "On E012", but their times (6.45 s and 7.26 s) show they actually ran on the tip.

The biggest new finding is E025: Muon on the block conv filters beat SGD by +0.78 pp, the opposite of what the hypothesis tree expected. But it cost +0.81 s, almost all of it per-step launch overhead (~2.3 ms per step).

**Top priority (5): turn Muon into speed.**
- **I032** keeps the Muon math identical but makes it cheap: same-shape filters run through one batched Newton-Schulz, and the whole Muon step goes inside the captured train-step graph. Expected time is ~6.65-6.85 s.
- **I033** spends Muon's gain on fewer epochs, cutting from 11 to 9.5. Expected accuracy is ~0.755, at ~6.27 s on the current Muon code or ~5.8 s if I032's fused version works. Either would be a new best.

**Other exploit ideas:**
- **Batch 2048 (priority 4):** a further throughput gain of -2 to -4% expected, with some risk of losing accuracy.
- **Whole-phase CUDA graphs (priority 2):** removes the host gaps between graph replays; -3 to -6% expected.

**Explore ideas, each one cheap and decisive:**
- **Whitening-bias training cut from 3 to 0.5 epochs (priority 3):** a schedule constant left over from 37-epoch runs; costs no time.
- **Max + average pooling before the head (priority 2):** a near-free test of whether the 100-class head is limited by its feature dimension.
- **Block 3 widened from 704 to 896 (priority 2):** a dose-response point for the block-3 width lever.

The literature committee's forecasts gave no votes on queued ideas, so none could be sharpened or dropped on that basis.

The noise floor (H1.1.3) is handled by a rule in I033: any new tip that clears 0.753 by less than 0.3 pp is rerun and pooled before it replaces E024. That matters because per-trial accuracy on the same seed varies by up to 0.9 pp between runs.

H4.2.1 should be marked supported, overturning its "expected: refuted" note. H4.2's confidence should go up, and its statement should be rewritten to say Muon wins on CIFAR-100.
